BiblicalUsage: Na'aq means to groan, and it is the sound of the wounded, not the sound of complaint. In Ezekiel 30:24 Pharaoh groans before the king of Babylon with the groanings of a deadly wounded man, and in Job 24:12 men groan from out of the city while the wounded cry out.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God hears a groan as a prayer, even when the groaning one has no words left; the wounded do not have to explain themselves to be heard.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
